paragraph: Cresskill is a single-family town first. Forty-four houses closed over six months at a median of $1,317,500, with a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00, about 43 percent selling above asking, and a median of 20 days on market. That is competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes are moving quickly, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones, but sellers are not dictating terms across the board. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with three full baths, though capes and split-levels show up regularly. Prices run from $698,000 to $4,299,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. The monthly series tracks the normal seasonal arc on volume: thin February through May, then 11 closings in June and 16 in July. Those two months are the only ones with enough sales to read, and their medians came in at $1,335,000 and $1,475,000. If Cresskill follows the usual pattern, expect closings to taper modestly through fall before deep winter thins out. Townhouses are a small slice, five sales at a median of $940,000, mostly three-bedroom units that went in about two weeks. Five sales cannot carry a trend claim, but the demand is clearly there. If you're weighing the two, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a townhouse.
